text:
Conclusions
Leveraging conventional material selection frameworks that are 
focused on performance and material price, and which are already 
familiar to materials scientists and engineers, to consider ENMs and 
their environmental and human health impacts will be increasingly 
important as the ENM enterprise continues to develop and mature.

metadata.title: A framework for sustainable nanomaterial selection and design based on performance, hazard, and economic considerations

entities.text: The data necessary to systematically assess safety before commercialization are lacking
simultaneous consideration of functional performance, price and environmental impact

An adapted framework based on the Ashby material selection strategy is presented as an enhanced selection and design process, which includes functional performance as well as environmental and human health considerations.
The utility of this framework is demonstrated through two case studies, the design and selection of antimicrobial substances and conductive polymers
Development and implementation of this framework can inform decision-making for the implementation of ENMs to facilitate promising applications and prevent unintended consequences.

text:
The systematic selection strategy presented here offers multi-fac-
eted practical benefits including (1) selecting the optimum sub-
stance considering a variety of attributes (for example, performance, 
environmental and human health implications, price of materials) 
from the currently available ENM, chemical and material libraries, 
(2) addressing real or perceived risks, and (3) avoiding regrettable 
substitution.

text:
This framework brings value to the material selection 
process, and supports curation of the ever-expanding nanomaterial 
library focusing limited resources on the most promising ENMs. 
 Further, there are broadly transformative impacts of the proposed 
framework, such as highlighting data gaps to motivate critically 
needed research and developing tools to inform the design of ENMs 
and ENM-enabled products.
